key_points.point: The document argues that we must embrace the current crisis as a catalyst for revolutionary change rather than succumbing to catastrophism. By identifying the 'increasing automation in production processes' as a core driver of the capitalist crisis, it suggests that the path forward lies in liberating productive forces. This aligns with the accelerationist goal of using technological advancement to build a post-capitalist future. It acknowledges the climate crisis but subordinates it to the necessity of transforming industrial policy.
key_points.verbatim: The “Manifesto for an Accelerationist Politics” (MAP) opens with a broad acknowledgment of the dramatic scenario of the current crisis: Cataclysm. The denial of the future. An imminent apocalypse. But don’t be afraid! ... What is at the center of the Manifesto is “the increasing automation in production processes,” including the automation of “intellectual labor,” which would explain the secular crisis of capitalism.
key_points.excerpt_context: Introduction, paragraphs 1-2

key_points.point: The author advocates for a strategy of 'within and against,' where the liberation of labor potential occurs through the evolution of capitalism itself. By pursuing technological development and economic growth, we can provoke a reversal of class relations. This reflects the accelerationist method of using the system's own momentum to reach a breaking point. It emphasizes that we must not confuse acceleration with mere speed, but rather treat it as an experimental engine for discovery.
key_points.verbatim: Its hypothesis is that the liberation of the potentiality of labor against the blockage determined by capitalism must happen within the evolution of capitalism itself. It is about pursuing economic growth and technological evolution... in order to provoke a complete reversal of class relations.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section: Within and Against the Tendency of Capitalism, paragraph 1

key_points.point: The text calls for the reappropriation of fixed capital, specifically focusing on the material and technical qualities of the technosocial body. It argues that cognitive labor must be liberated from capitalist command by mastering the tools of production, such as algorithms and mathematical models. This supports the accelerationist value of democratizing and repurposing advanced tools. It notes that the use of these tools by capital does not make them inherently capitalist.
key_points.verbatim: The first element is what I would call the “reappropriation of fixed capital” and the consequent anthropological transformation of the working subject. ... The use of mathematical models and algorithms by capital does not make them a feature of capital. It is not a problem of mathematics—it is a problem of power.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section: The Reappropriation of Fixed Capital, paragraphs 1-2

key_points.point: The document emphasizes the need for a new institutional transition that moves beyond horizontalism and spontaneous movements. It argues that planning is essential for revolutionary transformation, shifting from state command to a network-based convergence of productive capacities. This aligns with the accelerationist vision of building new, post-capitalist institutional forms. It acknowledges that planning the struggle must precede the planning of production.
key_points.verbatim: When it comes to revolutionary transformation, we certainly cannot avoid a strong institutional transition, one stronger than any transition democratic horizontalism could ever propose. ... planning the struggle comes before planning production.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section: Within and Against the Tendency of Capitalism, paragraph 3

key_points.point: The author highlights the necessity of acquiring the highest techniques of capitalist command, including algorithmic machinery and global logistics, to turn them into tools for communist administration. This reflects the accelerationist argument that we must master the system's complexity to transcend it. It frames this as a Promethean and humanist politics that embraces scientific potential. It cautions that this requires a collective effort to build new worlds.
key_points.verbatim: It is not a problem of mathematics—it is a problem of power. ... An Enlightenment aspiration—“the future needs to be constructed”—runs through the entire Manifesto. A Promethean and humanist politics resounds as well.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section: The Reappropriation of Fixed Capital, paragraph 2; Section: An Ecology of New Institutions, paragraph 2

key_points.point: The text argues for the construction of a new intellectual infrastructure to support ideal projects and the study of new economic models. It calls for organizing initiatives on the terrain of mass media and the internet to reclaim communication means. This supports the accelerationist method of building hegemony through technological and informational control. It stresses the importance of assembling and hybridizing all existing experiences of class power.
key_points.verbatim: First of all, building a new kind of intellectual infrastructure to support a new ideal project and the study of new economic models. ... A unitary constitution of class power will be possible only through the assemblage and hybridization of all experiences developed so far.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section: An Ecology of New Institutions, paragraph 2

key_points.point: The document advocates for a new positive humanism that goes beyond the limits of capitalist society, reviving dreams of space exploration and overcoming the accidents of life. This aligns with the accelerationist goal of using technology to expand human potential. It emphasizes the need for rational imagination and collective fantasy to organize new worlds. It frames this as a necessary step for the self-valorization of labor.
key_points.verbatim: A Promethean and humanist politics resounds as well. Such a humanism, however, going beyond the limits imposed by capitalist society, is open to post-human and scientific utopias, reviving the dreams of twentieth-century space exploration or conceiving new impregnable barriers against death and all the accidents of life.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section: An Ecology of New Institutions, paragraph 2

key_points.point: The author notes that the hegemony of immaterial labor is now established, marking a shift from Fordist production. This cognitive labor is the class that must be liberated to drive revolutionary change. This supports the accelerationist focus on cognitive labor as the primary productive force. It acknowledges that this class is endowed with higher power, making it the key to future hegemony.
key_points.verbatim: we have to finally grasp the shift from the hegemony of material labor to the hegemony of immaterial labor. ... It is the class of cognitive labor. This is the class to liberate, this is the class that has to free itself.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section: Within and Against the Tendency of Capitalism, paragraph 3

key_points.point: The document argues that the network must replace vertical state command, converging productive and directional capacities. This supports the accelerationist preference for decentralized, networked power structures. It frames this as a task for further elaboration, emphasizing that planning the struggle is the primary objective. It rejects the idea that horizontalism alone is sufficient for revolutionary change.
key_points.verbatim: According to the MAP, such “planning” no longer constitutes the vertical command of the state over working class society; rather, today it must take the form of the convergence of productive and directional capacities into the Network.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section: Within and Against the Tendency of Capitalism, paragraph 3

key_points.point: The author asserts that there is no 'outside' to globalization, meaning we must bring the 'outside' in to breathe life into the 'inside.' This aligns with the accelerationist strategy of operating within capitalist structures to transform them. It emphasizes the necessity of bringing the potentiality of the outside into the current capitalist reality. It frames this as a way to breathe powerful life into the system.
key_points.verbatim: The most modern epoch that we have experienced has shown us that there is nothing but an Inside of globalization, that there is no longer an Outside. Today, however, reformulating again the issue of reconstructing the future, we have the necessity—and also the possibility—of bringing the Outside in, to breathe a powerful life into the Inside.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section: An Ecology of New Institutions, paragraph 2

key_points.point: The document defends the term 'accelerationism' despite its unfortunate connotations, arguing that it captures the necessity of traversing the tendency of capitalist development to its end. This supports the accelerationist method of pushing the system to its breaking point. It clarifies that this is not about futurism, but about a rupture that leads to a communist program. It frames this as a decisive leap forward for revolutionary reflection.
key_points.verbatim: The name “accelerationism” is certainly unfortunate, as it ascribes a sense of “futurism” to something that is not at all futuristic. The document is undoubtedly timely... It posits, with extreme strength, the issue of the tendency of capitalistic development, of the need for both its reappropriation and for its rupture.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section: On the Thresholds of Technopolitics, paragraph 2

key_points.point: The document acknowledges the 'dramatic scenario of the current crisis' and the threat of an 'imminent apocalypse.' This aligns with the safetyist focus on catastrophic risks that threaten humanity's future. It emphasizes that the current crisis is not just a political issue but a systemic one that could lead to a total collapse of the future. It frames the situation as a cataclysm that requires a decisive response.
key_points.verbatim: The “Manifesto for an Accelerationist Politics” (MAP) opens with a broad acknowledgment of the dramatic scenario of the current crisis: Cataclysm. The denial of the future. An imminent apocalypse.
key_points.excerpt_context: Introduction, paragraph 1

key_points.point: The author criticizes the 'complete paralysis of the political imaginary' and the 'obstruction of productive capacities' by capitalist command. This aligns with the safetyist concern that current systems are unable to manage the risks posed by rapid technological change. It suggests that without a systematic approach, we cannot escape the current crisis spontaneously. It calls for a radical alternative to the status quo.
key_points.verbatim: Under these conditions, the future appears to have been cancelled by the imposition of a complete paralysis of the political imaginary. We cannot come out of this condition spontaneously. Only a systematic class-based approach... will make possible the reconstruction of hegemony.
key_points.excerpt_context: Introduction, paragraph 3

key_points.point: The document emphasizes the need for a 'constitutive apparatus' that aims to break the 'repressive and hierarchical horizon' of state-supported capitalism. This aligns with the safetyist value of ensuring that powerful systems are subject to human-defined constraints. It argues that we must oppose biopower with biopolitics to ensure an emancipatory future. It frames this as a necessary step for revolutionary reflection.
key_points.verbatim: It represents a decided and decisive leap forward—necessary if we want to enter the terrain of revolutionary reflection. But above all, it gives a new “form” to the movement, with “form” here meaning a constitutive apparatus that is full of potentiality, and that aims to break the repressive and hierarchical horizon of state-supported contemporary capitalism.
key_points.excerpt_context: Introduction, paragraph 4

key_points.point: The text warns against the 'distorted' nature of current financial and political systems, which it describes as having 'insuperable limits.' This aligns with the safetyist view that current institutions are inadequate for managing the risks of advanced technology. It argues that we must move beyond horizontalism to build stronger, more effective institutional transitions. It frames this as a task of planning for the future.
key_points.verbatim: Obviously, new illusions of centralism and empty reinterpretations of the “proletarian dictatorship” are not repeated by the authors. The MAP grasps the opportunity to clarify this by proposing a sort of “ecology of organizations,” insisting on a framework of multiple forces that come into resonance with each other.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section: An Ecology of New Institutions, paragraph 1

key_points.point: The document identifies the 'increasing automation in production processes' as a cause of the secular crisis of capitalism. This aligns with the safetyist concern that rapid automation can lead to systemic instability. It argues that capitalism has had to react to and block the political potentiality of post-Fordist labor, creating a crisis. It highlights the need to address these structural issues to prevent further destabilization.
key_points.verbatim: What is at the center of the Manifesto is “the increasing automation in production processes,” including the automation of “intellectual labor,” which would explain the secular crisis of capitalism. ... capitalism had to react to and block the political potentiality of post-Fordist labor.
key_points.excerpt_context: Introduction, paragraph 1; Introduction, paragraph 2

key_points.point: The author calls for a 'unitary constitution of class power' through the assemblage and hybridization of all experiences developed so far. This aligns with the safetyist goal of creating robust, coordinated oversight mechanisms. It emphasizes that this is a necessary task for the future. It frames this as a way to build a strong, collective defense against capitalist command.
key_points.verbatim: A unitary constitution of class power will be possible only through the assemblage and hybridization of all experiences developed so far, and those yet to be invented.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section: An Ecology of New Institutions, paragraph 2

key_points.point: The text highlights the need for 'rational imagination' accompanied by 'collective fantasy' to organize new worlds. This aligns with the safetyist value of proactive, imaginative risk management. It argues that we must go beyond the limits imposed by capitalist society to conceive of new, safer futures. It frames this as a necessary step for the self-valorization of labor.
key_points.verbatim: Rational imagination must be accompanied by the collective fantasy of new worlds, organizing a strong self-valorization of labor and society.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section: An Ecology of New Institutions, paragraph 2

key_points.point: The document insists on the need to 'break the relentless progression of productive tension' and identify the 'thresholds of development.' This aligns with the safetyist goal of setting clear, enforceable limits on AI capabilities. It argues that without such consolidations, a political program is impossible. It frames this as a way to avoid methodological helplessness.
key_points.verbatim: We have to break the relentless progression of productive tension on which the Manifesto relies. We have to identify the thresholds of development and the consolidations of such thresholds... Without such consolidations, a political program... is impossible.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section: On the Thresholds of Technopolitics, paragraph 2

key_points.point: The author argues that we must 'specify what the common is' in any technological assemblage. This aligns with the safetyist value of clearly defining and governing the shared resources that AI relies on. It emphasizes the need for a specific study of the anthropology of production. It frames this as a way to ensure collective control over technological development.
key_points.verbatim: We need to specify what the common is in any technological assemblage, while developing a specific study of the anthropology of production.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section: On the Thresholds of Technopolitics, paragraph 3

key_points.point: The document calls for the 'refusal of labor' as a way to adjust the time at the service of automatons. This aligns with the safetyist goal of ensuring that AI systems do not dominate human life. It argues that we must enforce drastic reductions of labor time and institute a base income. It frames this as a way to ensure equal participation in collective wealth.
key_points.verbatim: The struggle against algorithmic automation must positively catch the increase of productivity that is determined by it, and then it must enforce drastic reductions of the labor time disciplined or controlled by machines and, at the same time, it must result in consistent and increasingly substantial salary increases.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section: The Currency of the Common and the Refusal of Labor, paragraph 2

key_points.point: The author emphasizes the need to 'open up another theme': the production of subjectivity and the agonistic use of passions against capitalist command. This aligns with the safetyist focus on the psychological and social impacts of AI. It argues that we must organize a strong self-valorization of labor and society. It frames this as a way to counter the command of capital.
key_points.verbatim: And, at this point, we should not forget to open up another theme: the production of subjectivity, the agonistic use of passions and the historical dialectics this opens against capitalist and sovereign command.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section: The Currency of the Common and the Refusal of Labor, paragraph 2

key_points.point: The document identifies the 'increasing automation in production processes' as a primary cause of the current capitalist crisis. It argues that this automation is being used to block the political potential of post-Fordist labor. This aligns with the skeptic concern about labor displacement and the concentration of power. It emphasizes that the crisis is a result of neoliberal aggression against class relations.
key_points.verbatim: What is at the center of the Manifesto is “the increasing automation in production processes,” including the automation of “intellectual labor,” which would explain the secular crisis of capitalism. ... capitalism had to react to and block the political potentiality of post-Fordist labor.
key_points.excerpt_context: Introduction, paragraphs 1-2

key_points.point: The author critiques the current Left for being deceived by 'impossible' Keynesian resistance and failing to imagine a radical alternative. This aligns with the skeptic view that traditional political responses are inadequate for the scale of AI-driven economic change. It calls for a systematic class-based approach to reconstruction. It frames the current situation as a complete paralysis of the political imaginary.
key_points.verbatim: This is followed by a harsh criticism of both right-wing governmental forces, and of a good part of what remains of a Left—the latter often deceived (at best) by the new and impossible hypothesis of a Keynesian resistance, unable to imagine a radical alternative.
key_points.excerpt_context: Introduction, paragraph 3

key_points.point: The text argues that the current movements opposing financial capital lack proper tools and alternatives, despite their genuine revolutionary content. This aligns with the skeptic critique that current resistance is insufficient to address the structural power of AI-driven capital. It suggests that we need stronger institutional transitions. It frames the current movements as having insuperable limits.
key_points.verbatim: Obviously, new illusions of centralism and empty reinterpretations of the “proletarian dictatorship” are not repeated by the authors. The MAP grasps the opportunity to clarify this by proposing a sort of “ecology of organizations,” insisting on a framework of multiple forces that come into resonance with each other.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section: An Ecology of New Institutions, paragraph 1

key_points.point: The document critiques the 'repressive and hierarchical horizon' of state-supported contemporary capitalism. This aligns with the skeptic concern about the concentration of power in AI-driven systems. It calls for a new form of organization that breaks this horizon. It frames this as a necessary step for revolutionary reflection.
key_points.verbatim: But above all, it gives a new “form” to the movement, with “form” here meaning a constitutive apparatus that is full of potentiality, and that aims to break the repressive and hierarchical horizon of state-supported contemporary capitalism.
key_points.excerpt_context: Introduction, paragraph 4

key_points.point: The author notes that cognitive labor is ontologically valorized but devalorized from a monetary and disciplinary perspective. This aligns with the skeptic concern about the devaluation of human work in the face of AI. It argues that this class of cognitive labor must be liberated. It frames this as a fundamental issue of class struggle.
key_points.verbatim: It is the class of cognitive labor. This is the class to liberate, this is the class that has to free itself. ... ontologically valorized (it increases the production of value), yet devalorized from the monetary and disciplinary point of view.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section: Within and Against the Tendency of Capitalism, paragraph 2

key_points.point: The document argues that planning the struggle must come before planning production. This aligns with the skeptic view that political organization is necessary to counteract corporate control of AI. It rejects the idea of vertical state command. It frames this as a convergence of productive and directional capacities into a network.
key_points.verbatim: The following must be taken as a task to elaborate further: planning the struggle comes before planning production. ... planning no longer constitutes the vertical command of the state over working class society; rather, today it must take the form of the convergence of productive and directional capacities into the Network.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section: Within and Against the Tendency of Capitalism, paragraph 3

key_points.point: The author insists on the importance of acquiring the highest techniques of capitalist command to bring them back to a communist administration. This aligns with the skeptic goal of reclaiming technological power from corporations. It frames this as a problem of power, not just mathematics. It emphasizes that we must mature the productive potentialities of cognitive labor.
key_points.verbatim: It is not a problem of mathematics—it is a problem of power. ... we first have to mature the whole complex of productive potentialities of cognitive labor in order to advance a new hegemony.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section: The Reappropriation of Fixed Capital, paragraph 2; Section: An Ecology of New Institutions, paragraph 1

key_points.point: The document calls for activating all institutional forms of class power, both global and local. This aligns with the skeptic focus on building collective power to challenge corporate dominance. It emphasizes the need for a unitary constitution of class power. It frames this as a way to hybridize all experiences developed so far.
key_points.verbatim: A unitary constitution of class power will be possible only through the assemblage and hybridization of all experiences developed so far, and those yet to be invented.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section: An Ecology of New Institutions, paragraph 2

key_points.point: The author argues that we must bring the 'outside' in to breathe life into the 'inside' of globalization. This aligns with the skeptic critique of the totalizing nature of capitalist command. It frames this as a necessary step for reconstructing the future. It emphasizes that there is no longer an outside to globalization.
key_points.verbatim: The most modern epoch that we have experienced has shown us that there is nothing but an Inside of globalization, that there is no longer an Outside. Today, however, reformulating again the issue of reconstructing the future, we have the necessity—and also the possibility—of bringing the Outside in, to breathe a powerful life into the Inside.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section: An Ecology of New Institutions, paragraph 2

key_points.point: The document critiques the 'distorted' nature of financial capital and its extraction of value from society. This aligns with the skeptic concern about the financialization of AI and its impact on the economy. It calls for a communist program to attack this extraction. It frames this as a way to anticipate the attack on the measure of labor.
key_points.verbatim: Such a monetary abstraction, as a tendency of the becoming-hegemonic of financial capital itself, also points to potential forms of resistance and subversion at the same highest level. ... The communist program for a postcapitalist future should be carried out on this terrain.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section: The Currency of the Common and the Refusal of Labor, paragraph 1

key_points.point: The author advocates for the 'refusal of labor' as a way to enforce drastic reductions in labor time and salary increases. This aligns with the skeptic goal of protecting workers from the negative impacts of AI automation. It frames this as a way to ensure equal participation in collective wealth. It emphasizes the need to claim this through struggle.
key_points.verbatim: The struggle against algorithmic automation must positively catch the increase of productivity that is determined by it, and then it must enforce drastic reductions of the labor time disciplined or controlled by machines and, at the same time, it must result in consistent and increasingly substantial salary increases.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section: The Currency of the Common and the Refusal of Labor, paragraph 2

factual_claims.claim: The 'Manifesto for an Accelerationist Politics' (MAP) was published in 2013 by Alex Williams and Nick Srnicek.
The 'One divides into Two' formula originated in Maoist China in the 1960s as a critique of political recomposition with capitalism.
The 'tendency of the rate of profit to fall' is a concept from Karl Marx's Capital, volume 3, chapter 13.
Mario Tronti introduced the concept of the 'social factory' in his 1962 essay 'La fabbrica e la società'.
In political economy, 'fixed capital' traditionally refers to money invested in fixed assets like buildings and machinery, while 'circulating capital' includes raw materials and wages.
The current global cycle of struggles, characterized by horizontalism and spontaneous organization, began in 2011.
Marx defined the social force of cooperation as the surplus produced by workers working together, which is greater than the sum of their individual efforts.

unmapped_concepts.suggested_description: The idea that our bodies and social structures are becoming increasingly integrated with technology, creating new forms of collective power and potential. It emphasizes that we don't yet know the limits of what this hybrid existence can achieve.
unmapped_concepts.concept: The document refers to the 'modern technosocial body' as a site of potentiality, arguing that we are only beginning to understand the collective power that can be harnessed through the reappropriation of fixed capital and the transformation of labor power.
unmapped_concepts.reason: This concept frames technological integration as a source of revolutionary potential rather than just a tool or a risk.

unmapped_concepts.suggested_description: The principle that political organization and the planning of class struggle must precede the planning of economic production. It argues that without a strong political foundation, attempts to manage production are doomed to fail or be co-opted.
unmapped_concepts.concept: The author explicitly states that 'planning the struggle comes before planning production,' emphasizing that revolutionary transformation requires a strong political organization that can direct productive capacities toward post-capitalist ends.
unmapped_concepts.reason: This concept provides a specific methodological priority for revolutionary change that is distinct from purely economic or purely political approaches.
The concept of 'within and against' describes a strategy of operating inside capitalist structures to transform them, which is interpreted differently by all three camps.
unmapped_concepts.Accelerationist Interpretation: Using capitalist development and technological growth as an engine to reach a breaking point and trigger a post-capitalist transition.
unmapped_concepts.Safetyist Interpretation: A dangerous strategy that risks accelerating systemic failures and catastrophic outcomes before adequate safety and control mechanisms are in place.
unmapped_concepts.Skeptic Interpretation: A necessary but insufficient tactic that must be coupled with strong political organization and worker power to prevent co-optation by corporate interests.
